assets.prompt: A single isolated medieval guild coat of arms on a transparent background. PNG clipart with alpha transparency. Square canvas. The complete coat of arms is a pointed heater shield, deep forest-green field, black outline, thin old-gold border. Inside it: a large ivory medieval closed tournament helmet in side profile above a crossed gold feather quill and ivory blunt tournament lance. Flat heraldic woodcut style, bold simple shapes, discreet aged paper-like texture inside the shield, exactly three symbols, restrained muted colors. The crest is centered, entirely visible with a small empty margin. No words, no scene. Transparent background.

Subject: On a deep dark teal simple pointed heater shield with a restrained old-gold inner border, a large elegant ivory horse head in heraldic profile is framed by an open gold horseshoe. A single gold quill crosses the lower opening of the horseshoe. The mane uses just a few broad flowing black lines. The visual meaning is horse breeding and equestrian writing. Horse head is clearly dominant, quiet balanced compact design with only horse, horseshoe and quill; no saddle, crown, scroll, knights or extra symbols. Deep teal, ivory, muted old gold and black.

Period wool and linen clothes, modest tailoring, no modern suit, sports jersey, camera, microphone, printed modern logos, machinery, glasses or readable text. Scene: At the outer rail of a medieval tournament ground in a grand old neutral city, a youthful newspaper lad aged 17 energetically offers a folded sports gazette. Fair skin, short softly wavy dark-blond hair brushed back beneath a small forest-green cloth cap, warm grey eyes, expressive eyebrows, an open speaking mouth of natural size and cheerful intelligent expression; an original softly angular adolescent face. He wears a forest-green wool jerkin, cream linen collar, ochre short shoulder cape and a plain leather satchel strap. Waist-up view, one hand presenting a paper with a simple tournament helmet woodcut, other arm holding a small bundle. Behind him, slightly simplified wooden tournament rails, two distant pennants, spectators and weathered monumental stone arches from a vanished empire integrated into a living medieval town. No real-world landmarks. Morning light, forest green, cream, old gold. The boy and his expression dominate, background competition only a hint.

Scene: Inside the tournament-reporting guild's elevated timber writing gallery overlooking a distant medieval training yard, a refined stern male master aged about 50 instructs one male and one female student aged 18. All three waist-up around a small oak writing desk, faces clearly visible. Master: fair skin, long narrow composed face, iron-grey hair neatly brushed to the nape, short tidy dark-grey beard, forest-green embroidered wool robe, ivory collar, a modest old-gold chain of office, visibly elite and exacting but not cruel. Boy: fair skin, short chestnut hair with a neat side part, soft square jaw, attentive eyes, simple green apprentice tunic, holds a quill over an orderly score ledger. Girl: fair skin, honey-blond hair braided close at the back, rounded oval face, thoughtful expression, cream blouse and muted olive overdress, holds a sketch sheet showing two tiny full-body tournament stances as study figures. Master points to the inked results while explaining how to turn observation into a precise report. One small wooden practice weapon rests on a wall hook in the quiet background; no active fighting, gore or threatening pose. Filtered daylight, warm wood and forest-green palette, hands and faces legible.

Scene: A polite youthful newspaper seller aged 17 offers an illustrated equestrian magazine at a prosperous medieval horse fair. Fair-skinned Western European boy with smooth youthful face, short straight light-brown hair swept gently sideways beneath a small dark-teal cloth cap, green-grey eyes, a proportionate straight nose and a restrained warm closed-mouth smile. He wears a dark-teal wool vest over ivory linen, plain leather shoulder strap and a modest brown short cape. Waist-up framing with face, upper torso and paper fully clear. Over the boy's shoulder one calm elegant bay horse shows its anatomically correct head and upper neck from a timber stall, framed by neat stable rails and a pale canvas fair awning. Boy remains the main subject. Gentle morning sunlight, teal, cream, warm saddle-brown, refined rural atmosphere, no modern equestrian equipment.

Scene: A handsome distinguished male master of horse illustration aged about 52 teaches a male and a female pupil aged 18 in an airy medieval stud-farm drawing room beside a stable. All human characters fair-skinned Western European and original. Master: silver-brown hair parted and neatly tied at nape, fine short pointed beard, long composed face, sharp observant eyes, high-quality dark-teal doublet with modest gold embroidered edging and ivory collar; an elite exacting teacher. Boy: light chestnut hair in soft short waves, fine youthful oval face, teal apprentice vest, holding an open horse-pedigree notebook. Girl: dark-blond hair in a low braid, a distinct softly square youthful face, pale sage overdress over ivory linen, carefully drawing a horse's side profile with a quill at an angled wooden drawing board. The master points with one relaxed hand to the angle of the drawn shoulder. Through a quiet open stall window a single gentle bay horse's head and upper neck provide a live model. A simple leather bridle hangs on one peg, no clutter. Upper-body and face focus; students both engaged, no romance. Soft clear daylight, teal, pale sage, cream and warm oak. No named lore person is depicted.
